purpose: Trace the flyingfish-prey statement in the 2016 Batanes NSAP paper to its cited NOAA/FAO synthesis, identify the geographic and sample limits, and prevent a North Carolina stomach-content figure from being presented as Batanes diet or bait guidance.

source.title: Synopsis of the biological data on dolphin-fishes, Coryphaena hippurus Linnaeus and Coryphaena equiselis Linnaeus
source.publisher: NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service; FAO Fisheries Synopsis
source.publication: NOAA Technical Report NMFS Circular 443; FAO Fisheries Synopsis No. 130; April 1982
source.citation: Palko, B. J., Beardsley, G. L., & Richards, W. J. (1982). Synopsis of the biological data on dolphin-fishes, Coryphaena hippurus Linnaeus and Coryphaena equiselis Linnaeus. NOAA Technical Report NMFS Circular 443; FAO Fisheries Synopsis No. 130.
source.access: NOAA repository metadata and FAO-hosted full-text PDF reviewed. NOAA metadata lists Public Domain. No local PDF or figure retained.
source.license: Public Domain according to NOAA Institutional Repository metadata.

inputSource.claimAsReported: The 2016 Batanes marine fishery assessment describes flyingfish as favored prey of Coryphaena hippurus and points to Rose (1966) through Palko et al. (1982).
inputSource.limitation: This is a citation chain in the Batanes assessment, not a Batanes stomach-content observation or a result of its NSAP landing-data analysis.

northCarolinaSample.locationAsReported: off the coast of North Carolina, USA
northCarolinaSample.resultAsReported: Flyingfish (Exocoetidae) made up almost 25% of total food-item weight in the summarized sample.
northCarolinaSample.figureLineage: NOAA/FAO Figure 8 caption attributes the stomach-content chart to Rose (1966), figure 26. The surrounding prose also references Rose and Hassler (1974). The original Rose thesis was not independently accessed or reviewed.
northCarolinaSample.interpretationLimit: Historical regional sample result; not a universal prey proportion and not evidence from Batanes or the Philippines.

contrastingGulfStreamSample.resultAsReported: The synthesis lists 32 fish species from 19 families, a crab, a shrimp, four cephalopods, and Sargassum; flyingfish were not found in that sample.
contrastingGulfStreamSample.interpretationLimit: A different historical sample with a different prey composition; supports retaining regional/sample variation.

findings.lifeStageContext: The synthesis says diet changes during growth and summarizes larvae of dolphin-fishes as feeding mainly on crustaceans, especially copepods. This is background from a multi-species, multi-source synthesis, not a Batanes larval survey.
findings.sourceScope: The reviewed report synthesizes studies from multiple regions including the Atlantic and Pacific. The particular nearly-25% flyingfish result is explicitly North Carolina, not Philippine waters.

nextAction: Seek direct Philippine or Batanes diet evidence before adding local food-preference content. Keep any future species diet statements tied to their source location, sample, and life stage, and keep diet separate from bait recommendations.
